content: 1. When co-administering drugs that are substrates of OCT2 or MATE transporters, monitor for substrate-related toxicities. If co-administration cannot be avoided, consider reducing the dosage of the co-administered drug based on its product labeling. 2. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor the effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates when co-administered. 3. Both telavancin and trimethoprim increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Trimethoprim and telmisartan both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially at high doses, in patients with renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 5. Trimethoprim decreases thiamine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but should be monitored. 6. Thioridazine and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of tovorafenib by reducing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining tovorafenib, a CYP2C8 substrate, with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 8. Trimethoprim and trandolapril both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, particularly at high doses, in patients with renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 9. Trazodone and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Trimethoprim and triamterene both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia. Triamterene increases trimethoprim levels or effects due to competition for renal tubular clearance. The interaction mechanism is unspecified, and the clinical significance is unknown. 11. Trifluoperazine and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Trilaciclib decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining trilaciclib, an OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K inhibitor, with substrates where even minimal concentration increases in the kidney or blood may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 13. Trimipramine and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Tropisetron and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of tucatinib. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib increases trimethoprim levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid combining tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 16. Trimethoprim decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 17. Valsartan and trimethoprim both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, particularly at high doses, in patients with renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 18. Venlafaxine and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of verapamil due to competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but should be monitored. 20. Voclosporin and trimethoprim both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Voriconazole and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Trimethoprim increases zidovudine levels by reducing its renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for potential increased toxicity. 23. Ziprasidone and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Prolonged use of trimethoprim may cause fungal or bacterial superinfections, including Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea and pseudomembranous colitis, which can occur more than two months after antibiotic treatment. 25. Trimethoprim may cause hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, maculopapular rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Use caution in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 26. Trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, preventing the reduction of folic acid to tetrahydrofolate, thereby inhibiting microorganism growth. It is extensively distributed in body tissues and fluids, crosses the placenta, and enters breast milk. Its half-life is prolonged in renal impairment. 27. Large doses or long-term therapy with trimethoprim may interfere with hematopoiesis, leading to conditions such as megaloblastic anemia, leukopenia, or thrombocytopenia. Monitor for early signs of blood disorders, such as sore throat, fever, pallor, or purpura. If significant reductions in blood cell counts are observed, discontinue the drug. 28. Trimethoprim is not indicated for prophylactic or prolonged use in otitis media at any age. It is classified as Pregnancy Category C and enters breast milk. Use caution in patients with potential folate deficiency, such as the malnourished, elderly, or those on chronic anticonvulsant therapy. Folates may be administered concomitantly without interfering with the antibacterial action of trimethoprim. 29. Some dosage forms of trimethoprim may contain benzyl alcohol and derivatives, which should be avoided in neonates.
